subject.title: fix(streaming): preserve paragraph separators across block-streamed deliveries [AI-assisted]

question: Should this PR be limited to the common in-band separator repair, or should maintainers require an explicit boundary-semantics contract that also preserves near-`maxChars` paragraph seams before merge?
rationale: The code path and bug are clear, but the remaining blocker is a maintainer-owned delivery contract choice that affects shared streamed-message semantics and the competing candidate PR.

options.title: Require complete boundary semantics
options.body: Choose one consolidated implementation that preserves paragraph seams for both in-budget and near-limit chunks before merging.

options.title: Accept partial common-case repair
options.body: Land the text-only improvement knowingly and leave the near-`maxChars` seam as remaining work on https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/42106.

options.title: Pause for metadata design
options.body: Ask for an explicit seam metadata design across chunker, subscriber, coalescer, and outbound delivery before either candidate proceeds.

recommendation.title: Require complete boundary semantics
recommendation.body: Choose one consolidated implementation that preserves paragraph seams for both in-budget and near-limit chunks before merging.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest combined history across block reply coalescing, chunking hardening, and the shared streaming boundary touched here.
